voiceover:
[conversational] One person runs this boring image API, and it makes $13K a month.

And the real move behind it happened before the product even existed.

[curious] It's called Orshot. You design a template once, then render images, PDFs and videos from it through an API. Agencies, brands and developers pay for it.

[confident] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR, through Stripe. $13K in MRR, $12K in the last 30 days, 225 active subscriptions, and 22% growth. Look at their pricing page: free with 100 credits, then $39 a month.

So how did it grow? Founder Rishi Mohan talked to customers constantly. He emailed a new signup, built the feature he needed, and that guy became a customer. Add patient SEO and honest comparison pages.

[serious] The honest catch? It's a crowded space, and Orshot's own blog admits it doesn't win on price per video. Also, revenue isn't profit.

[whispers] So here's the move. He built an audience first. The same crowd that backed his earlier product, Pika, gave Orshot its first users.

[playful] Steal that. Audience first, product second.

Would you build this or buy it? Send this to the friend who keeps saying they'll launch someday.

Hack saved?

topic: Business breakdown: Orshot.com — Orshot is an API and Automation service for Creative Marketing

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Orshot.com — Orshot is an API and Automation service for Creative Marketing
pick.angle: A tiny team makes $13K/month selling an API that auto-generates social media images and banners

research.what_it_does: An API and no-code automation platform. You design a template once in a browser editor, then render images, PDFs and videos from it via REST API, n8n, Make, Zapier or AI agents.
research.who_pays: Developers, agencies, brands and marketing teams that need to produce marketing visuals at scale. One example is CreatorCore, which runs influencer campaigns for agencies and music labels.
research.pricing: Official pricing page (orshot.com/pricing): Free with 100 credits/month (no card), Launch from $39/mo (1,500 credits), Grow from $160/mo (20,000 credits), Scale from $349/mo (75,000 credits). 1 credit = 1 image, 1 PDF page or 1 second of video. Enterprise is custom. TrustMRR also lists Social Publishing at $12/mo per social account (not checked on the pricing page).
growth: Building in public on X. Rishi says the same audience that gave his earlier product Pika its first users later gave Orshot its first users. He says many early users were developers and indie makers who followed him. Source: Fakemayo interview (~mid-2026).
Rishi says 'a good chunk' of Orshot's initial customers came from the Pika crowd. He adds that the rest came slowly, 'the boring way'. Source: Fakemayo interview.

SEO: Rishi credits 'patient, unglamorous SEO' plus building in public and reputation. His Pika product had crossed $100k in earnings 'just from SEO, building in public and word of mouth' before Orshot. Source: Fakemayo interview.
Orshot's own blog publishes many comparison pages, for example vs Bannerbear, Placid, APITemplate.io, Shotstack and Remotion. These carry pricing 'checked' dates in Aug–Oct 2026.

Direct customer outreach: Rishi emailed a new signup, asked about his use case, then built a tool for him (carousels auto-generated from Twitter threads). That user became a customer. Source: Rishi's LinkedIn post.
Rishi's 1-year post says he focused mainly on talking to customers about their use cases and learning from them. Source: orshot.com/blog/1-year-orshot.
When the Pika API was retired in favor of Orshot, Rishi reached out directly to some Pika API customers and helped them migrate. CreatorCore was one of them. Source: Orshot blog, Aug 24, 2026.
Product Hunt: Orshot's page lists 5 launches, including May 7, 2025, June 12, 2025 and March 16, 2026. Source: Product Hunt page. No upvote or ranking figures were found.
founder_story: Rishi Mohan is a solo founder. Orshot is run through his company DaSkrad, and in his own 1-year post he says he has been 'solo building' it. A mid-2026 interview said it was 'still just me'.

Before Orshot he built Pika (pika.style, screenshots and mockups), which started in January 2022 as a side project. His LinkedIn says he has 8+ years in design and frontend engineering. His site lists previous roles at Borg, BigBinary and Instahyre.
In the Fakemayo interview Rishi says he started building Orshot in February 2025, registered DaSkrad and launched it the same month. TrustMRR lists the founding date as March 2025.
He says it took roughly a year to get past 100 customers. He names Incubeta and Brendi as customers, saying Brendi handles marketing for over 5,000 restaurants.
He publishes numbers on orshot.com/open (not opened or checked).
lessons: Build your audience before the product. Rishi's years of building in public gave Pika its first users and then Orshot's. His X following is 7,544 per TrustMRR.
Talk to your first users. Rishi emailed a signup, learned the need, built the feature for him and turned him into a customer.
Reuse an existing product's customers. When Rishi retired the Pika API, he reached out to its customers directly and helped them move to Orshot.
Use SEO comparison pages ('X alternative') that include honest pricing tables. Orshot's own pages concede where competitors are cheaper, for example Placid and Imejis.
criticism: Crowded category with established rivals: Bannerbear, Placid, APITemplate.io, Shotstack, Creatomate and Remotion. Orshot's own blog admits it 'doesn't win on price per video'.
The entry plan is not the cheapest. Imejis.io's comparison puts Launch at $0.026 per image, versus Imejis.io's $0.015. Orshot's own Placid page says Placid is cheaper on raw credits from Pro up.

Credits reset monthly and do not roll over, per Orshot's own Placid comparison. Overage is pricey (video overage is 8 credits per second per the docs; imejis.io cites $36 per 1,000 extra renders on Launch).
Revenue is not profit. No cost or profit data was found. A solo founder also means key-person risk.
Pricing has changed. A third-party review (imejis.io) says Orshot restructured pricing in 2026, and Software Advice still shows old plans ($30/$160/$480). Use only the current pricing page.
Third-party review presence is thin (G2 and Capterra), per checkthat.ai. That page's claim of no Product Hunt listing is wrong, since a PH page exists.
facts: Orshot's 1-year post (published about 230 days before today) says '350k+ Renders and 100+ Customers'.
Fakemayo interview (about 122 days old): around 5,000 users, about $6.2K MRR and 760k+ renders so far.

TrustMRR (Stripe-verified): MRR is now $13,169 with 225 active subscriptions. That is roughly double the $6.2K MRR figure from the interview, which is a different date, so only compare them with care.
Free plan: 100 credits/month. Videos are capped at 30 seconds on Free, 3 minutes on Launch, 5 on Grow and 10 on Scale, per the Orshot blog.
Outputs: PNG, JPG, WebP, PDF, MP4, WebM and GIF from one template, drawing on one credit pool (Orshot blog).
Orshot features posting to 15 social platforms from the render call (Orshot blog) and an embeddable Studio editor (Rishi's X post).

Pricing comparison, from the Bannerbear and imejis.io comparisons: Grow works out to about $0.008 per image and Scale to about $0.0047, which imejis.io calls the cheapest bulk rates in its comparison.
do_not_claim: Team size beyond 'solo', which is sourced from the founder as of mid-2026
Any specific Product Hunt ranking or upvote count for Orshot
That Orshot got a 'viral moment'. None was found.
How many customers came from SEO versus X versus Pika. The founder gives no split.
Founder location: TrustMRR says United Kingdom, but the founder's own sources say Berlin, Germany. Avoid stating it.
Founding month: TrustMRR says March 2025, but the founder says he started building in February 2025. Use 'early 2025'.
Exact count of the founder's prior Pika revenue beyond 'crossed $100k in earnings', which is the founder's own claim.
Funding: no funding round was found.
research.notes: The pricing page snippets show Launch at $39 and Grow at $160 in the same layout. Check the live page for the exact on-screen text before recording. The 'show' strings are taken from search snippets and blog titles, not from a live page view. Verify 'Automate Image, PDF & Video Generation via API' on the homepage. It matches the TrustMRR value proposition and appeared as the homepage H1 in search results. Orshot's blog pricing claims are written by the company itself, so treat competitor comparisons as marketing. The $6.2K MRR figure (Fakemayo, about 4 months old) conflicts in time with today's $13,169 MRR from TrustMRR. Do not describe it as the current figure. For the video hook, the strongest sourced angle is that a solo founder used build-in-public, SEO and direct customer conversations, starting from an audience built with a previous product (Pika).
